research_question: In which occupations and labour markets does the cost of accepted output fall faster than workers can gain experience, find comparable paying work and recover earnings?
assumptions_and_limits: US hiring and same-platform estimates cannot be transferred directly to Brazil. Brazilian figures are published results, with no new linked occupation-series estimates asserted.
The aggregate, firm, occupation, cohort, platform and experimental units are kept separate. Scenario arithmetic is illustrative.
counterfactuals: Continued increases in inexperienced hires at comparable pay in exposed jobs, improved unaided skills and recovered net freelance rates would weaken the concentrated entry-loss hypothesis.

Stable formal youth hiring shares in Brazil, near-zero measured effects in Danish records, and concentrated senior growth rather than outright junior contraction at foreign affiliates qualify the thesis.

producer_checks.scope: Bilingual occupation-by-occupation analysis with 52 numbered references per locale, two source-based charts, a geographic comparison, a mechanism flow and evidence tables.
producer_checks.source_vintage: November 2026 material includes the ILO brief, software postings, affiliate event study and freelance marketplace study.
producer_checks.independence: Staged for the independent editorial QA gate.
